stem: Which statements correctly describe Massachusetts LTC emergency-kit safeguards? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each Schedule II-V unit should be tamper-evident/resistant and individually packaged as a single dose
A facility may use an ADD instead of the traditional locked box when relevant requirements are met
Schedule VI emergency doses remain subject to procurement, storage, dispensing, administration, recording, and disposal controls
Schedule VI emergency stock is exempt from the facility quality-assurance process
Once a kit is approved, controlled-substance accountability policies are optional

explanation.core_reasoning: LTC emergency kits combine package integrity, accountability, Schedule VI controls, and an optional compliant ADD format.

choice_analysis.A: The circular specifies that package form.
choice_analysis.C: Schedule VI does not escape accountability.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule VI use is monitored by the QA/assessment committee.
choice_analysis.E: Security and accountability policies remain required.

related_facts: Facilities need not stock every allowed item or the maximum quantity.
explanation.mpje_trap: Assuming emergency access relaxes controlled-substance safeguards.

reasoning_steps: Separate packaging, device, and Schedule VI obligations
